tools.name: ask_audience
tools.title: Ask One Standalone Audience Question
tools.description:
Asks exactly one standalone question of one existing Audience. It creates a private Study for that Audience, starts asynchronous answers from its Minds, and returns the Study identifier and its links.

The server may reword a context-dependent question. The accepted task and its answer contract are returned with the original request. Ambiguous requests or generated questions return planning_required before execution.

Out of scope: a questionnaire, battery, section or any request with two or more known questions. That complete set runs as one planned multi-question block inside a Study.

Attachments can be URLs, Minds uploads or files shared in the conversation (uploaded or generated images, PDFs).

audience.description: Which Audience to ask. Give the id when known, otherwise the name.

id.description: Audience ID (UUID). Preferred when known.

name.description: Audience name: exact or partial (case-insensitive), with a fuzzy fallback for typos.

question.description: Exactly one respondent-visible standalone question for every Mind in the Audience. The system may classify or reformat it, but any text in this field can reach the Minds and influence their answers. Include only the question and the instructions the Minds should receive. Material the question is about (a pasted newsletter, email, ad copy or concept text) goes in textAttachments, verbatim, not here. Never place planner-only or MCP-client orchestration instructions here. If the question offers a fixed set of answer options, say so in the text as the respondent would read it. The research reader identifies the question and its answer contract together. Include the complete authored labels, ordering and selection instructions. Numbered answer options do not by themselves make a request a multi-question battery. An invalid or ambiguous reading stops for retry or planning before execution.

name.description: Optional name for the Study created to ask this question. Defaults to the Audience name.

attachments.description: Files/images processed once and given to every Audience member as context. Accepts a public HTTP(S) URL or a file already in the user's Minds uploads under chat/<userId>/ (its storage path or its /api/uploads/chat/ URL). MCP cannot read a local path. Files shared in the conversation (uploaded or generated images, PDFs, documents) go in the tool's top-level conversationFiles field where the tool has one; elsewhere a PDF or image without a public URL has no MCP route and is uploaded in the Minds app first. Plain text contents (UTF-8 text, Markdown, CSV, JSON) can go to import_audience_sources. External URLs are copied into Minds storage before a Study is saved or run. temp/, portfolio/ and context/ paths and /api/uploads/file-access/ URLs belong to other owners and are not accepted. A Study does not start until Minds can read every file.

tools.name: create_audience_from_brief
tools.title: Create a Grounded Audience from a Brief
tools.description: Researches a free-text population brief and builds a new Audience of Minds with explicit profiles and exact segment allocation. A new brief returns an evidence-backed draft for review; creation requires the user-accepted draft or quota snapshot and its checksum. A change to a draft under review is a draft.rework of that draft, never a new brief, which leaves another open draft. Recalibrate an existing Audience by its id. Supports reviewed respondent datasets. Creation is asynchronous and returns an operation ID. Audiences are private unless link sharing is enabled.

draft.description: The webapp Audience draft workflow. Preview proposes Minds before Create; id and sha256 identify the exact reviewed roster. Rework revises that draft in place: every change the user asks for while reviewing it (size, market, wording, an axis to drop, a file to add) is preview:true with this id and sha256 and the change as rework, never a new brief. The brief may be omitted on a rework; any option sent with it, such as composition.memberCount or research.files, replaces the draft's stored one. Set preview:false with both id and sha256 only after the user confirms the displayed draft; that confirmation needs nothing else (omit the brief and every other option): the server creates exactly the reviewed draft from its stored request.

brief.description: Free-text brief describing the population the Audience should represent. E.g. "California high school students grades 9-12", "Berlin Späti customers", "Spanish lawyers", "management team of Coca Cola". The server runs deep web research on this brief to find demographic / psychographic distributions from authoritative sources, then generates personas that proportionally reflect those distributions.

name.description: Optional Audience name override. When omitted, the server names the Audience from the brief or the LLM detection result.

operationId.description: Resume a queued preview or creation by its returned jobId. Reads its v1 operation status without creating or charging anything. Supply this alone; do not repeat the creation brief to check progress. Once the creation completed, the result also says whether every Mind can chat yet (the Audience is ready then) and how many are still learning from their sources in the background; call it again to follow that.

isLinkSharingEnabled.description: Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asked for a public/shareable link. Defaults to false: the Audience is private to its owner and no share URL is generated. Enabling this publishes the Audience — including its grounding, sources and personas — at a world-readable URL that needs no login. Do not enable it to "be helpful".

research.description: Extra material the grounding research reads alongside the brief, and whether web search runs at all.

links.description: Optional URLs scraped server-side for additional context (e.g. an article describing the population).

keywords.description: Optional Exa web-search seeds added alongside the brief.

files.description: Optional already-uploaded research files. Accepts a public HTTP(S) URL or a file already in the user's Minds uploads under chat/<userId>/ (its storage path or its /api/uploads/chat/ URL). MCP cannot read a local path. Files shared in the conversation (uploaded or generated images, PDFs, documents) go in the tool's top-level conversationFiles field where the tool has one; elsewhere a PDF or image without a public URL has no MCP route and is uploaded in the Minds app first. Plain text contents (UTF-8 text, Markdown, CSV, JSON) can go to import_audience_sources. External URLs are copied into Minds storage before a Study is saved or run. temp/, portfolio/ and context/ paths and /api/uploads/file-access/ URLs belong to other owners and are not accepted. A Study does not start until Minds can read every file. The server analyzes these through the same extended screener/questionnaire path as the in-app New Audience uploader, including study roles, screening and quota rules, review distributions, and grounding provenance. Every file shapes the grounding, but only one classified as supporting material (not a spreadsheet) enters the members' own knowledge; the result's withheldFromMemberKnowledge names each other file with its reason (respondent_dataset, study_report, questionnaire, screener, distribution_source, tabular, or unclassified: not classified as supporting material, also when the reading failed or ran out of time).

name.description: File name

url.description: URL of an already-uploaded file. Accepts a public HTTP(S) URL or a file already in the user's Minds uploads under chat/<userId>/ (its storage path or its /api/uploads/chat/ URL). MCP cannot read a local path. Files shared in the conversation (uploaded or generated images, PDFs, documents) go in the tool's top-level conversationFiles field where the tool has one; elsewhere a PDF or image without a public URL has no MCP route and is uploaded in the Minds app first. Plain text contents (UTF-8 text, Markdown, CSV, JSON) can go to import_audience_sources. External URLs are copied into Minds storage before a Study is saved or run. temp/, portfolio/ and context/ paths and /api/uploads/file-access/ URLs belong to other owners and are not accepted. A Study does not start until Minds can read every file.

includeWebSearch.description: Set false to skip Exa web search and extraction completely. The Audience is then grounded only on the brief and supplied files, links, keywords, and structurally parsed respondent data. Note that a study report, questionnaire, screener or respondent dataset grounds the Audience but is deliberately withheld from the members' own knowledge, so it cannot be the evidence they answer from; with nothing else to ground on, the Audience is still created from the brief and its charts and says that its members carry no readable evidence. Leave it true unless the supplied sources include material the members themselves should read.

composition.description: How many Minds to create and how the cohort is allocated across the grounded axes.

memberCount.description: Exact number of Minds to create. Pass this whenever the user states a size ("exactly 50 per region", "genau 50 Minds je Zelle") instead of relying on the server to parse the number out of the brief. When omitted, the size is inferred from the brief and, failing that, from the creation mode's evidence-based automatic sizing. The only refusal is 403 PLAN_LIMIT above your plan's per-Audience cap. The 6000 accepted here is the absolute system ceiling, not your allowance — call get_audience_limits for the real one before you propose a size, and offer the user the sizes it allows. The Audience is never created at a partial size.

audienceCreationMode.description: How the Audience is sized. "balanced" (default): compact and representative for everyday research. Its automatic sizing stops at 20 Minds; a larger memberCount moves to a deeper mode when your plan includes one, otherwise "balanced" builds it, up to your plan's per-Audience allowance. "segment_coverage": two representatives per limiting grounded cell, from a 10-Mind floor; automatic sizing stops at 50, but a memberCount you state is bounded only by your plan. "benchmark_depth": repeated representation of limiting grounded cells for validation-ready segmentation; bounded by your plan allowance. The deeper two are included only on some plans (get_audience_limits shows which apply to you) — on other plans the server SILENTLY downgrades to "balanced" and echoes the effective mode in structuredContent.audience.audienceCreationMode. Call get_audience_limits to see the ceilings that apply to your account.

cohortAllocation.description: Deterministic allocation controls. Reviewed respondent datasets default to observed, which preserves the strongest privacy-safe structural relationships while keeping exact marginals; other sources default to independence. Use distributionNames/maxDistributions to choose axes, minSegmentCount for a feasible floor, and seed for reproducible external runs.

datasetSegmentation.description: Which variables of a respondent dataset shape the cohort. A draft whose research.files include a respondent dataset (XLS, XLSX, CSV, SPSS .sav; Pro plan, audienceCreationMode="benchmark_depth") reads it and proposes this selection itself; its review lists every variable with its role and observed shares. Omit this on the first draft. To change the variables, revise that draft (draft.preview:true with its id and sha256, the same brief and research.files) passing {fileName, sheetName, segmentationColumns} from the review with the keys the user chose. Structural variables shape one representative cohort; outcomes stay held out.

fileName.description: The dataset's file name, as the draft's datasetSegmentation review names it. The same file must be in research.files (or conversationFiles).

segmentationColumns.description: Keys of the variables the user kept after review. These are the only ones that shape the cohort.

respondentCount.description: Legacy: total respondent rows in the reviewed sheet. Omit with a selection.

recommendedMindCount.description: Legacy: preview-recommended cohort size, which caps the cohort. Omit with a selection.

variables.description: Legacy: variable-level distributions (preferred over `columns` when present). Omit with a selection.

columns.description: Legacy: column-level distributions, used when `variables` is absent. Omit with a selection.

combinations.description: Legacy: observed joint profiles as audit counts. Omit with a selection.

excludeDistributions.description: Exact axis names whose composition quotas should be removed. Age remains as one eligibility range without within-range shares; explicit gender membership remains enforced. Include required eligibility axes in cohortAllocation.distributionNames. Original evidence stays in reviewDistributions.

trainMembers.description: Deprecated; omit it. Every member of every Audience is trained individually in the background, including reviewed-dataset cohorts of more than ~40 Minds (each keeps its deterministic cohort profile and the request locale). true is accepted as a no-op; false is rejected, because it used to create untrained Minds with an empty system prompt that reported ready. Cost and time: one Mind training per member; a 100-Mind cohort takes tens of minutes to a few hours. The tool returns as soon as the Audience exists (structuredContent.audience.memberTraining reports what was queued); wait until every member reports readyToChat (readiness.isReady when this tool is called again with the returned operationId) before running a Study, which refuses Audiences with untrained members; the Audience is ready at that point. Members keep learning from their sources in the background for a few more minutes (readiness.learning, then readiness.fullyTrained); nothing needs to wait for it. readyToChat means the member can answer, not that it researched anything: a member whose collection found nothing keeps one generated context item and still reports ready, so check knowledgeState.fallbackOnly on the members before treating the Audience as evidence-backed.

grounding.description: Review the quota axes before any Mind exists, and pass a reviewed snapshot back unchanged to create from it.

preview.description: Review the quota axes BEFORE any Mind exists. When true, the server runs research grounding and deterministic cohort allocation without creating an Audience or Minds or consuming a generation allowance. To revise a saved preview without repeating research, pass its unchanged reviewedGroundingJson/SHA pair together with groundingPreview and the revised exclusion/allocation options. Fresh research uses the same durable operation as the public REST API; this tool returns its operation immediately so the widget can stream sources and distributions. New briefs, including respondent datasets, default to the full webapp draft with proposed Minds; only a legacy full dataset payload uses a quota-only review. Setting false without reviewed evidence still returns a preview. Present the plan and wait until the user confirms it, then set grounding.preview:false with the unchanged reviewedGroundingJson/SHA pair and the same allocation options. Supplying saved evidence without an explicit false keeps it in review. The response includes effective target percentages and integer counts; explicit allocation targets that do not match grounded axes are set aside and listed in cohortAllocation.audit.warnings (or as a target_unapplied notice on the grounding), never refused. If research did not finish, the preview says so (research_unavailable) and creating from it researches the Audience in the background.

reviewedJson.description: Exact reviewedGroundingJson returned by groundingPreview or import_audience_sources. Pass it unchanged together with reviewedGroundingSha256 on a re-preview or creation call; the server reuses this reviewed snapshot instead of rerunning grounding research.

reviewedSha256.description: SHA-256 returned by the same groundingPreview. Required together with reviewedGroundingJson; any mismatch is rejected before Audience or Mind materialisation.

conversationFiles.description: Research files (screener, questionnaire, report, respondent data), read like research.files. Files shared in this conversation: uploaded or generated images, PDFs, documents. Each is copied into Minds storage on receipt; its file_id is its attachment id.

readiness.description: When a completed operation is read back: member rollup from GET /api/v1/audiences/{id}/progress. isReady = every Mind can chat (the Audience is ready); startsNow = a Study started now runs at once, without leftOut Minds whose training failed for good; learning = ready Minds still learning from their sources in the background; fullyTrained = none still learning; research.phase = researching while the Audience's background research runs (it is usable meanwhile), researched once merged and applied.

tools.title: Create a Study
tools.description:
Creates a Study workspace from existing Audiences or inline Audience configurations. It does not ask questions or run research, and follow-up research inside an existing Study needs no new Study.

A Study with this exact name is named back and nothing is created, unless allowDuplicateName is true; work in that Study instead. Studies cannot be deleted here, so any extra Study is permanent.

Any request with two or more known questions belongs in one planned and confirmed multi-question block inside the Study, submitted once rather than as separate direct questions.

Creation is atomic and rolls back partial Audience failures. Studies are private; enabling link sharing also publishes the attached Audiences and their Minds. It cannot publish, share or replace an existing Study: that sharing changes only in the workspace.

Enabling this ALSO publishes every attached Audience and every Mind inside them at world-readable URLs — including pre-existing Audiences passed via audienceIds. Do not enable it to "be helpful".

tools.title: Create Study Plan
tools.description: Creates a non-executing draft in an existing Study with its Audiences already attached. The setup operation for two or more known questions: every question known now belongs in this one draft, in cohesive named modules. A one-question draft is only for genuinely standalone research or an adaptive follow-up. request designs questions; questions preserves a fixed instrument verbatim. Each Mind sees only its own earlier answers; askIf applies respondent-level skip logic. With multiple attachments, stimulus.questionAttachments assigns each question; [] means none. Saving bounded history may prune older revisions. Research has not started; the returned draft revision needs review and later explicit confirmation.

study.description: Study id or name. Omit to use the active Study of this MCP session.

id.description: Existing Study UUID. Takes precedence over name.

name.description: Existing Study name when no ID is given. Omit both references to use the active Study.

request.description: Planner input containing the research objective, questionnaire, survey, battery, section, cohesive question set, audit request, or analysis request. Required for a new draft. Include EVERY question already known in this one request so the planner can group the complete set into cohesive named modules for one confirmed multi-question run inside the Study; never create one planning request per known question. This request is not sent verbatim to Minds; the exact proposed respondent-visible questions are returned in the draft for review. Write only the user's research brief and context relevant to the research question. Never tool errors, status or retry messages, Minds or other internal links, or your own process notes.

questions.description: Fixed instrument: use INSTEAD of request when the user supplies a pre-registered or fixed questionnaire whose wording, order, and response formats must not change. The planner is bypassed; every question is stored verbatim, in this order, with exactly this response contract. Cannot be combined with refinement, answers or questionResponses in the same call (refused); suggestQuestionStimuli has no effect here, place files with questionAttachments; answer the draft's confirmation questions afterwards with draft.id, draft.revision and draft.answers alone, which keeps these questions exactly. Repeated question texts or colliding ids are rejected. A saved Study template's configuration.questions can be passed here (each item's text and response); pass its configuration.methodId as policy.methodId so the template's method runs. Without it a fixed instrument runs as Custom research (guided-research).

id.description: Stable item id (lower-cased to a slug). Defaults to q<position>.

text.description: Exact respondent-visible question text, including any anchors or labels. Stored as given. Answer options do NOT belong here: list them in response.categoricalOptions instead. A question whose text spells out its choices but is typed qualitative is answered as free text, every Mind converges on the same most likely wording, and the chart shows one option at 100%. State the options here only as a respondent would read them, and always carry the same options in response.categoricalOptions so the contract and the wording agree. Skip and filter instructions ("No -> go to Q12", "only if Q3 = Yes") do not belong in the text either: transcribe each as askIf. A jump from an answer of item G to item N gives every item between G and N answerNotIn [that answer]; a filter gives answerIn. Tell the person about any instruction you cannot map to exact items and options instead of guessing it.

module.description: Optional module (battery) label. Consecutive questions with the same label form one module.

code.description: ISO 4217 currency code (EUR, USD); % for percentage; singular Intl unit identifier (hour, meter, kilogram, liter) for measurements; or a label of up to 80 characters for custom. Selecting a unit does not convert numbers or impose a range.

scalePoints.description: Exhaustive allowed scale answers in authored order, each with its literal label and numeric value. Omit for an unenumerated range; never fill missing intermediate points.

scaleRange.description: Inclusive finite numeric response bounds as [minimum, maximum], only when specified. Numeric responses may be unbounded. Fractional and wide ranges retain their authored values.

categoricalOptions.description: Predefined answer choices; only valid for categorical, multiselect or ranking responses. A ranking orders all of them.

maxSelections.description: Maximum choices a respondent may select; only valid for multiselect responses.

response.description: Exact execution contract for this item. Pick by what the question asks of a respondent: a fixed set of choices is categorical (exactly one) or multiselect (several, with maxSelections); putting every option in order is ranking; a numeric judgement is scale with an inclusive finite numeric scaleRange; only a genuinely open answer in the respondent's own words is qualitative. categorical, multiselect and ranking all carry the choices in categoricalOptions, which keep their exact labels and order even with attachments; files are evidence and do not generate replacement A/B options.

askIf.description: Routing: ask this item only of respondents whose own answer to an earlier item (questionId) matched. Give exactly one of: answerIn or answerNotIn with an earlier categorical or multiselect item's exact option labels; or categoryIn or categoryNotIn for an earlier open (qualitative) item, whose answers are coded into the categories named for it (one frame per item, at most 12) once it has been answered; an answer fitting none of them counts as none. Scale and ranking items cannot gate. Respondents not asked are recorded as not asked and excluded from this item's results.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional stable retry key. When omitted the tool derives one from its own arguments, so a repeated identical call (including a host retry after a timeout) returns the draft revision that was already saved instead of planning again. Pass a fresh key to force a new plan for identical input.

Accepts a public HTTP(S) URL or a file already in the user's Minds uploads under chat/<userId>/ (its storage path or its /api/uploads/chat/ URL). MCP cannot read a local path. Plain text contents (UTF-8 text, Markdown, CSV, JSON) can go to import_audience_sources. tools.name: get_audience_limits
tools.title: Get Audience Limits
tools.description:
Returns the authenticated account's current plan (`planName`, as the app names it), its Audience size allowance (per-Audience cap including any team or contract allowance, `customSizeMax`, per-mode ceilings) and the synthetic responses left, read live; it supersedes limits stated elsewhere. Sample sizes the plan allows: up to `customSizeMax` Minds per Audience, or several Audiences in one Study for a larger sample, each costing one response per Mind per question.

`automaticSizingCeiling` bounds the size the server picks when memberCount is omitted; `explicitCountCeiling` is the stated size above which a deeper mode builds it (only "balanced", on plans with one); otherwise `memberCap` alone bounds a stated size. Sizes are per Audience for the account and team named, not a reservation.

planName.description: The plan name the customer sees in the app. Use it, not the tier key in `plan`.

tools.name: get_study_status

Returns Study progress, per-Audience results, original Mind responses, links and export status. In-flight questions report zero Minds answered until completion; partial per-Mind progress is not persisted. questionId selects one question; runId selects a confirmed run with question-level counters. Without either, results cover the entire Study. Values and labels are written in the Study display locale, returned as locale: the language of its confirmed plan, else the stored Study locale, else English.

tools.name: recalibrate_audience
tools.title: Change an Existing Audience
tools.description: Changes an existing Audience in place: it keeps its id, its Minds keep theirs (except copies below), and no Mind is deleted. Covers composition and trait edits, a population pivot, adding members, an exact chart selection (`distributions`), new sources and going deeper (`deepen`), and re-runs its research grounding. Owner, or verified Minds staff with existing direct Audience admin collaboration or an active owner-issued support grant. Staff support is limited to composition amendments: no growth, new sources, Go deeper or shared-Mind waiver. Asynchronous: the result is an accepted operation with its id, not a completed change. Queues behind another edit of the Audience and waits for a Study run on its members. Members shared with other Audiences are replaced here by copies with new ids. Reusing requestKey with identical input retries safely.

audience.description: Which existing Audience to change. Give the id when known, otherwise the name.

id.description: Audience ID (UUID). Preferred when known.

requestKey.description: Stable retry key. Reuse with identical input to recover the same recalibration operation, including its completed result.

research.description: What to change and the evidence for it. Omit it (and distributions/deepen) to re-run the research from the original brief.

instruction.description: The change the user wants, folded into the replayed original brief. Its reach decides how members change: a composition edit ("make men 40%", "add an income distribution") re-allocates only members whose segment changed; a trait change ("now they are all vegan", "SMB owners instead of enterprise buyers") evolves members in place (same name and portrait, rewritten profile, knowledge retrained); a population pivot ("now Gen-Z students instead of retirees") rebuilds every member in place with a new persona, portrait and knowledge; an additive instruction ("and now add 10 African consumers") adds new members within the plan limits and leaves the others untouched; a stated total for the same people ("make it 10", "reduce to 10 people") keeps the members who best hold the Audience's composition (and any member named or said to keep, "keep Anna", "keep the CEO"; a member named to remove, "drop Anna", always leaves; a name several members carry decides nothing and the result's notes say so) and removes the rest from this Audience only (their Minds stay in the library, nobody is retrained), and asking for a copy or version ("a 10-person version") leaves this Audience as it is and makes a copy holding those members (the completed result's `resize` names who was kept and left out); anything else in the same instruction ("make it 10 and add an income chart", "20 more, and make women 60%") is applied right after, once, while wording that only preserves ("do not change their facts") starts nothing. The parts are read by a model in any language and checked against the instruction's own words; an instruction that cannot be read in full changes nothing and is retried automatically (`AUDIENCE_EDIT_UNREAD` while queued). Mind ids never change and no Mind is deleted. Use this, not query, to adjust the Audience.

requestedDistribution.description: Exact topic that must materialize as a new distribution, alongside instruction, when the user explicitly asks to add one. Without research evidence it is added as an assumption and flagged as such. Other charts and targets stay; an existing one that states the same personal fact (for example personal and household income whose brackets cannot be compared) stays as a chart, and the requested one is allocated in its place.

sources.description: Optional new first-party files, links, or keywords to add to the durable audience evidence before recalibration.

distributions.description: Optional exact active distribution selection from the grounding review. Supplying this uses selection mode and applies the user-authored composition directly, including exact shares: to set a chart to e.g. 70% Female / 30% Male, send the complete active set with that chart's `pct` values changed. They become the user's targets beside the evidence (shown as "Set by you"); no research runs and the members are re-allocated to them. Send each chart's stored `name`, `label` and `sourceIdx` from the Audience's stored grounding (structuredContent audience.grounding.distributions); the Audience's saved evidence is reattached to every chart and value it already has (names shown in the text output may be translated; use the stored ones). A chart or value it does not have yet (send `sourceIdx: -1`) is added as the user's target.

deepen.description: Go deeper, in the background: research what the Audience still lacks — every standard dimension its evidence reports missing or assumed, plus `topics` — and add it; every chart the Audience has stays, and stronger evidence replaces weaker only for the same question or dimension. Go deeper runs in the background and this tool returns at once; get_audience_creation_progress with the audienceId follows research.phase (researching, then researched). Not combinable with distributions, query or requestedDistribution. Asked while the Audience's background research is still running, it is queued behind that research and starts when it finishes.

tools.name: revise_study_plan
tools.title: Revise Study Plan
tools.description: Revises one saved draft at its current draft.id and draft.revision without starting research. Accepts edits, refinement, clarification answers or response-format corrections. Stale revisions fail. Fixed questions stay verbatim when only clarification answers change. Bounded history may prune older revisions; the changed draft requires review again.

request.description: Planner input containing the research objective, questionnaire, survey, battery, section, cohesive question set, audit request, or analysis request. Required for a new draft. Include EVERY question already known in this one request so the planner can group the complete set into cohesive named modules for one confirmed multi-question run inside the Study; never create one planning request per known question. This request is not sent verbatim to Minds; the exact proposed respondent-visible questions are returned in the draft for review. Write only the user's research brief and context relevant to the research question. Never tool errors, status or retry messages, Minds or other internal links, or your own process notes.

questions.description: Fixed instrument: use INSTEAD of request when the user supplies a pre-registered or fixed questionnaire whose wording, order, and response formats must not change. The planner is bypassed; every question is stored verbatim, in this order, with exactly this response contract. Cannot be combined with refinement, answers or questionResponses in the same call (refused); suggestQuestionStimuli has no effect here, place files with questionAttachments; answer the draft's confirmation questions afterwards with draft.id, draft.revision and draft.answers alone, which keeps these questions exactly. Repeated question texts or colliding ids are rejected. A saved Study template's configuration.questions can be passed here (each item's text and response); pass its configuration.methodId as policy.methodId so the template's method runs. Without it a fixed instrument runs as Custom research (guided-research).

id.description: Stable item id (lower-cased to a slug). Defaults to q<position>.

text.description: Exact respondent-visible question text, including any anchors or labels. Stored as given. Answer options do NOT belong here: list them in response.categoricalOptions instead. A question whose text spells out its choices but is typed qualitative is answered as free text, every Mind converges on the same most likely wording, and the chart shows one option at 100%. State the options here only as a respondent would read them, and always carry the same options in response.categoricalOptions so the contract and the wording agree. Skip and filter instructions ("No -> go to Q12", "only if Q3 = Yes") do not belong in the text either: transcribe each as askIf. A jump from an answer of item G to item N gives every item between G and N answerNotIn [that answer]; a filter gives answerIn. Tell the person about any instruction you cannot map to exact items and options instead of guessing it.

module.description: Optional module (battery) label. Consecutive questions with the same label form one module.

scaleRange.description: Inclusive finite numeric response bounds as [minimum, maximum], only when specified. Numeric responses may be unbounded. Fractional and wide ranges retain their authored values.

categoricalOptions.description: Predefined answer choices; only valid for categorical, multiselect or ranking responses. A ranking orders all of them.

maxSelections.description: Maximum choices a respondent may select; only valid for multiselect responses.

response.description: Exact execution contract for this item. Pick by what the question asks of a respondent: a fixed set of choices is categorical (exactly one) or multiselect (several, with maxSelections); putting every option in order is ranking; a numeric judgement is scale with an inclusive finite numeric scaleRange; only a genuinely open answer in the respondent's own words is qualitative. categorical, multiselect and ranking all carry the choices in categoricalOptions, which keep their exact labels and order even with attachments; files are evidence and do not generate replacement A/B options.

askIf.description: Routing: ask this item only of respondents whose own answer to an earlier item (questionId) matched. Give exactly one of: answerIn or answerNotIn with an earlier categorical or multiselect item's exact option labels; or categoryIn or categoryNotIn for an earlier open (qualitative) item, whose answers are coded into the categories named for it (one frame per item, at most 12) once it has been answered; an answer fitting none of them counts as none. Scale and ranking items cannot gate. Respondents not asked are recorded as not asked and excluded from this item's results.

tools.name: save_study_draft
tools.title: Save Study Draft
tools.description: Creates or checkpoints an unfinished Quick or Custom Study draft without starting research. It saves the objective, context, selected Audiences, method, questions, sources, and current planner step. Revisions change only the fields given and require the exact draft ID and expected revision; stale writes are rejected. For a retryable creation, choose idempotencyKey before the first save and reuse it after an uncertain result.

name.description: Sidebar name for the Study draft.

audienceIds.description: Existing Audience IDs selected for the Study. Preferred.

methodId.description: Research method selected for the draft. Use list_research_methods as the availability authority. When omitted on create, guided-research applies; when omitted on a revision, the saved method is kept.

questions.description: Manual research questions in their intended order. When omitted on create, the draft has none; when omitted on a revision, the saved questions are kept.

draft.description: Which durable draft to revise, and the retry key. Omit to create a new draft.

id.description: Existing Study draft ID to revise. Omit to create a new durable draft.

expectedRevision.description: Exact current revision. Required with draftId so stale updates cannot overwrite newer planning state.

idempotencyKey.description: Creation only: choose a stable key before the first save and reuse it after an uncertain result. Reuse returns the existing draft; use draftId and expectedRevision to change it.

planner.description: Planner state to restore when the draft is reopened.

mode.description: Planning mode to restore. When omitted on create, custom applies; when omitted on a revision, the saved mode is kept.

currentStep.description: Exact planner step to reopen, such as context, audiences, method, questions, or confirm. The legacy value groups remains accepted when reopening an older draft. When omitted on create, context applies; when omitted on a revision, the saved step is kept.

context.description: Research context captured so far: only the user's brief and material relevant to the research question, never tool errors, status messages, internal links or process notes.

objective.description: The user's research objective or intent captured so far. Never tool errors, status or retry messages, Minds or other internal links, or your own process notes.

notes.description: Research context the Minds should see: the brief, concept or other material relevant to the research question, and the user's constraints. When the draft starts, these notes are shown to every Mind. Never tool errors, status or retry messages, Minds or other internal links, or your own process notes.

website.description: Primary website associated with the research context.

sourceUrls.description: Ordered source URLs the user supplied as material for the research. Never Minds workspace or other internal links. When omitted on create, the draft has none; when omitted on a revision, the saved URLs are kept.

conversationFiles.description: Study context files for the draft: images, video and audio are stimulus respondents see, documents are background. They are kept on later saves of the same draft. Files shared in this conversation: uploaded or generated images, PDFs, documents. Each is copied into Minds storage on receipt; its file_id is its attachment id.

tools.name: start_study_heatmap
tools.title: Start Study Asset Heatmap
tools.description: Starts attention analysis of an assigned image, video or website. Uses one response per Mind and needs a paid plan. assetKey reuses completed analysis of that asset; omitting it may replace earlier derived results. Websites are visited publicly. Explicit approval is required; question answers are preserved.

tools.name: start_study_run
tools.title: Start Confirmed Study Run
tools.description: Runs one reviewed draft revision after explicit confirmation in a later user turn; skipping review is not confirmation. One execution submits the whole draft as a single durable run. It is refused as a whole before using Minds or quota if the revision, capabilities, method or source-readability checks fail. Advanced methods need explicit opt-in. Each Mind answers in order seeing its own earlier answers; askIf gates items. Contradictions are flagged, never rewritten.
